api.description:
`openai` only: the API; `None` is the Responses API without a
`base_url` and chat completions with one.

api_key_env.description:
The environment variable that holds the API key, and never the key.
`None` is `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for `anthropic` and no variable for
the others. The variable is withheld from every command, and its
value is cut out of every tool result.

base_url.description:
`anthropic` and `openai` only: where the API is served, for a
gateway or a local server. Its user information is a secret: cut
out of every tool result, and left out of the config digest.

cache.description:
`anthropic` only: whether requests carry cache breakpoints; `None`
is `true`.

cache_scope.description: Which runs share what the provider caches.

effort.description:
`anthropic`, and `openai` with the Responses API: the reasoning
effort.

max_tokens.description: The cap on output tokens for each call.

name.description: The provider's name for the model.

pricing.description: What the model's tokens cost, in US dollars per million.

provider.description: The provider the model is reached through.

reasoning_replay.description:
Chat completions only: whether reasoning is sent back; `None` is
`false`.

script.description: `fake` only: the file of scripted responses.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature, sent only when set.

thinking.description:
`anthropic` only: how the model is asked to reason; `None` is the
provider's default.

Otlp.description:
The `telemetry.otlp` section. A field that's `null` is the
environment's, read for each signal: the signal's own variable, else the
generic `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` one. The timeout, the compression and TLS
are the environment's alone.

enabled.description:
Whether a run exports over the network. `None` leaves each signal to
`OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` and `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, which turn it on
unless they're `none`. `true` turns both on and `false` both off,
whatever they say. `false` is refused beside a stated endpoint,
which it would make a setting without effect.

endpoint.description:
Where the collector listens. `None` leaves it to the signal's
variable and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, and then to the
protocol's default, `http://localhost:4318` or
`http://localhost:4317`. On HTTP it's a base URL, to which
`/v1/traces` and `/v1/logs` are appended. Its user information is a
secret, cut everywhere and out of the digest; set to nothing it
states none.

headers.description:
Headers sent with every export, and the only ones: none the
environment names is sent beside them, `{}` included. `None` sends
the environment's, wherever the endpoint came from. Every value is a
secret, written or substituted: a variable substituted into one is
withheld from every command, the value is cut out of every tool
result, and it's left out of the config digest.

protocol.description:
The protocol the collector is sent. `None` leaves it to the
signal's variable and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`, and then
HTTP/protobuf.

OtlpProtocol.description: The protocol an OTLP collector is sent, as the specification spells it.

oneOf.description: OTLP over gRPC.
OTLP over HTTP, as protobuf.
OTLP over HTTP, as JSON.

Half the cap from each end.

The JSON schema of the `task_complete` argument in explicit mode;
`None` takes any object.

context.description: What's sent of the conversation on each provider call.

max_consecutive_invalid_turns.description:
How many turns in a row may make no call that reached a tool; `None`
is no cap.

max_retries.description:
How many times a failed provider call is tried again; `0` never
retries.

max_total_tokens.description:
The budget of input plus output tokens, summed over every provider
call; `None` is no budget.

max_turns.description:
The cap on turns; `None` is no cap, and the timeout and the token
budget bound the run.

provider_timeout.description: How long one provider call may take, when the run has that long left.

retry_backoff_base.description: The wait after the first failed attempt, which doubles each time.

retry_hint_max.description: The longest wait a server may ask for; a longer one ends the retries.

retry_jitter.description: The largest share of a wait that's added to it, from 0 to 1.

timeout.description: How long the run may take.

transcript_format.description: The form the transcript is written in.

transcript_path.description:
Where the transcript is written when the run ends; it may hold
`{run_id}`. `None` writes none.

SkillsMode.description: How the model gets a skill's body.

oneOf.description:
The system prompt lists each skill, and a tool loads a body when the
model asks for it.
Every body follows the system prompt.

Telemetry.description:
The `telemetry` section. A field that's `null` is the environment's,
read as the OpenTelemetry specification reads it, and then the
specification's default; a field the config states wins.

capture_content.description:
Whether prompts, responses and tool content reach telemetry. `None`
leaves it to `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT`,
which turns it on only when it's `true` in any case.

resource.description:
The composer's own resource attributes, which every export carries.
They're stated over `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` and the attributes
`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` names, winning a key both name, and
`service.version` and the SDK's `telemetry.sdk.*` stay lablet's and
the SDK's whichever names them.

path.description:
The file every run's OTLP/JSON lines are appended to, or `-` for
standard error. `None` writes no file. No variable names one, and
the file gets both signals whatever the network does.

Thinking.description: How the model is asked to reason before it answers.

oneOf.description: Nothing is sent, so the provider's default applies.
The model decides how much to reason.
Reasoning is refused.

Reasoning is asked for with this many tokens to spend on it, which
is fewer than `max_tokens`.

allow.description:
The only tools offered, by the names the model sees; `None` offers
every tool.

deny.description: Tools that are never offered, by the names the model sees.

max_concurrent_calls.description: How many calls of one turn may run at once; 1 runs every call alone.

max_description_chars.description:
The length in characters above which a tool description or a
server's instructions are cut; `None` is no cap.

max_output_bytes.description:
The size in bytes above which a tool result is cut; `None` is no
cap.

mcp_lifetime.description: How long the MCP servers live.

mcp_result.description: Which part the model is sent of an MCP result that has two.

output_cut.description: What's kept of a result that's cut.

output_preview_bytes.description: How many bytes a preview keeps.

TranscriptFormat.description: The form a transcript is written in.

oneOf.description: The transcript document.
An ATIF trajectory.

description:
What a `Lablet` is built from.

The sections hold what the config states, as it's written, with
lablet's default wherever it states nothing and every provider shares
the default. A setting of the `model` section that's one provider's is
held as it was stated, and [`Config::resolved`] fills in its default.
`${VAR}` is held as it's written, and substituted when a `Lablet` is
built from the config or the config is checked.

Reading a config checks its shape. What a config may not state is
refused when it's checked, and when a `Lablet` is built from it.

run.description: How a run completes, what bounds it, and where its transcript goes.

telemetry.description: What telemetry captures, and where it's exported.

tools.description: The tools a run offers, and what bounds a call.
